note: Curated, hand-written knowledge base for the SIMULATED explanation of steganography algorithm selection. Not a learned model.

entries.title: LSB replacement (lsb_replacement)
entries.mechanics: lsb_replacement overwrites the least significant bit of each sample from sample 128 onwards with one payload bit, most significant bit first.
entries.capacity: Capacity is one bit per sample after the 128 bootstrap samples, the largest of the five algorithms.
entries.distortion: Each embedded bit changes a sample by at most 1, on average for half of the bits; this is the lowest distortion per embedded bit.
entries.cost: Cost is minimal: a single vectorised mask-and-or over the sample array, no image scan.
entries.limitations: lsb_replacement is fragile to JPEG, resizing and filtering and is statistically detectable (pairs-of-values asymmetry); it is not robust and not undetectable.
entries.keywords: lsb_replacement least significant bit replacement simple capacity distortion fragile detectable chi-square

entries.title: LSB matching (lsb_matching)
entries.mechanics: lsb_matching changes a sample by plus or minus 1 only when its least significant bit differs from the payload bit; direction comes from a deterministic seeded generator, with forced direction at 0 and 255.
entries.capacity: Capacity equals lsb_replacement: one bit per sample after the 128 bootstrap samples.
entries.distortion: Distortion is comparable to lsb_replacement but removes the pairs-of-values asymmetry that simple chi-square tests exploit.
entries.cost: Cost is low: one seeded random draw per payload bit and a vectorised update.
entries.limitations: lsb_matching is still fragile to JPEG, resizing and filtering and remains detectable by modern statistical steganalysis; it is not claimed robust.
entries.keywords: lsb_matching plus minus one matching random direction distortion fragile detectable steganalysis

entries.title: Pixel-value differencing (pvd)
entries.mechanics: pvd takes adjacent sample pairs, classifies the absolute difference into the ranges 0-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-63, 64-127 and 128-255 carrying 3, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 bits, and sets the new difference to the range start plus the payload value.
entries.capacity: pvd capacity depends on the cover: smooth areas carry few bits per pair and edges carry up to 7 bits per pair; capacity is exact and computed from the cover.
entries.distortion: pvd hides more bits in high-difference areas where changes are less visible, but individual samples can change by more than 1.
entries.cost: Cost is moderate: vectorised range lookup and cumulative sums over the pairs.
entries.limitations: pvd is fragile to JPEG, resizing and filtering; histogram steps at range boundaries make it statistically detectable, and it is not claimed robust.
entries.keywords: pvd pixel value differencing range table pairs capacity adaptive distortion fragile detectable

entries.title: Edge-adaptive LSB (edge_adaptive_lsb)
entries.mechanics: edge_adaptive_lsb computes a gradient mask from the 7 most significant bits and replaces least significant bits only in samples of pixels whose gradient reaches the threshold, default 6, so the receiver rebuilds the same mask.
entries.capacity: Capacity is the number of eligible edge samples, often a small fraction of the image; if the frame does not fit the algorithm is unavailable with EDGE_CAPACITY_INSUFFICIENT and there is no fallback to smooth pixels.
entries.distortion: Changes are confined to textured regions, which lowers visible distortion for a given payload.
entries.cost: Cost is moderate: gradient and mask computation scans the whole image.
entries.limitations: edge_adaptive_lsb is fragile to JPEG, resizing and filtering and is statistically detectable as an LSB-class method; low-texture covers give little capacity.
entries.keywords: edge_adaptive_lsb edge adaptive gradient mask texture threshold capacity eligible fragile detectable

entries.title: Block DCT quantisation (dct)
entries.mechanics: dct applies an 8x8 orthonormal DCT to one colour plane, and hides 6 bits per block by quantisation-index modulation of mid-frequency coefficients with step 12 by default, verifying each block after rounding.
entries.capacity: dct capacity is 6 bits per block, excluding the first block row, and is the smallest of the five algorithms.
entries.distortion: dct has the highest distortion of the five algorithms because coefficients move by up to a quantisation step.
entries.cost: Cost is the highest: forward and inverse block transforms with verification.
entries.limitations: dct is not claimed robust to JPEG or resizing in this implementation; saturated blocks at 0 or 255 can fail verification (ENCODE_VERIFY_FAILED), for example on black and white covers.
entries.keywords: dct discrete cosine transform block quantisation index modulation mid frequency distortion cost saturated verify

entries.title: Deterministic selector policy sel-policy-2
entries.mechanics: sel-policy-2 filters by capacity, trial-encodes each candidate on the real cover to measure MSE, PSNR and SSIM, applies hard limits, scores the rest with weights for distortion, utilisation and cost by priority class, and breaks ties inside an epsilon by a fixed order. sel-policy-2 applies the same rules to all ten algorithms.
entries.capacity: A candidate is excluded when its capacity is smaller than the frame.
entries.distortion: Hard limits are MSE and PSNR thresholds measured on the trial encode.
entries.cost: The cost term is a static model, not a measurement; wall-clock timings are reported but never ranked.
entries.limitations: The policy is a deterministic rule set, not a learned selector; the explanation text is generated after the decision and cannot change it.
entries.keywords: selector policy sel-policy-2 deterministic score weights priority tie break constraints mse psnr ssim eligible candidate reason

entries.title: PNG lossless handoff
entries.mechanics: The stego image is stored as PNG, re-opened and extracted again before the artifact id is returned; the receiver reads only the saved file.
entries.capacity: PNG adds no capacity limit of its own.
entries.distortion: PNG is lossless, so embedded bits survive exactly.
entries.cost: Encoding and re-reading the PNG is a small fixed cost.
entries.limitations: Any lossy transport such as JPEG, resizing, cropping or filtering destroys the payload; the handoff is lossless PNG only and none of the algorithms is robust.
entries.keywords: png lossless handoff file save reopen verify jpeg resize fragile transport artifact

entries.title: Capacity and utilisation
entries.mechanics: Capacity is the number of payload bits an algorithm can hide in the actual cover; the frame to hide is the Frame v1 header plus the encrypted AppWire plus the 32-byte authentication tag, plus a 16-byte bootstrap stored in the least significant bits of the first 128 samples.
entries.capacity: A candidate whose capacity is smaller than the frame is excluded before any trial encode; utilisation is frame bits divided by capacity bits and a lower value means the payload is spread thinly.
entries.distortion: Lower utilisation generally means fewer changed samples and therefore less distortion.
entries.cost: Capacity is computed from the cover and is exact for every algorithm; it costs a pass over the cover for pvd and edge_adaptive_lsb and is trivial for the LSB family.
entries.limitations: A long message can exceed the capacity of every algorithm on a small cover; the request then fails with a capacity error instead of truncating or falling back to plaintext.
entries.keywords: capacity utilisation frame bits payload size exclusion cover small large message insufficient bootstrap header

entries.title: Distortion metrics MSE, PSNR and SSIM
entries.mechanics: The selector trial-encodes every capacity-eligible candidate on the real cover and compares the result with the original cover to obtain MSE, PSNR in decibels and SSIM.
entries.capacity: Metrics are measured per cover and per frame, so the same algorithm gives different values on different covers or payload sizes.
entries.distortion: Lower MSE and higher PSNR mean a smaller visible difference; the default hard limits reject a candidate above MSE 4.0 or below PSNR 40 dB.
entries.cost: Measuring requires one trial encode per candidate, which is why the selector runs it only after the capacity filter.
entries.limitations: These are signal-fidelity numbers, not a measure of resistance to steganalysis; a high PSNR does not mean the embedding is undetectable.
entries.keywords: mse psnr ssim decibel metric distortion quality trial encode hard limit threshold visible difference fidelity

entries.title: Priority classes urgent, normal and background
entries.mechanics: The selector score is w_d times distortion plus w_u times utilisation plus w_t times estimated cost; the priority class sets the weights, urgent 0.2, 0.1 and 0.7, normal 0.5, 0.2 and 0.3, background 0.8, 0.15 and 0.05, and the lowest score wins.
entries.capacity: Utilisation enters the score as frame bits divided by capacity bits.
entries.distortion: Background messages weight distortion most heavily, so they favour the least visible embedding.
entries.cost: Urgent messages weight the static cost model most heavily, so they favour cheaper algorithms; the cost term is a model, not a timing.
entries.limitations: The weights are fixed by sel-policy-2 and are not learned or adjusted from past results.
entries.keywords: priority urgent normal background weights score w_d w_u w_t distortion utilisation cost class lowest score

entries.title: Tie-break order
entries.mechanics: When the best scores of several eligible candidates differ by no more than the tie epsilon, 0.01 by default, the selector picks the first of them in a fixed order: s_uniward, wow, hugo, lsb_matching, pvd, edge_adaptive_lsb, dwt, dct_svd, lsb_replacement, dct.
entries.capacity: The tie-break does not depend on capacity beyond eligibility.
entries.distortion: Because scores inside the epsilon are treated as equal, the tie-break can pick an algorithm with slightly higher distortion than the numerically best one.
entries.cost: No extra computation is needed; the order is a constant list.
entries.limitations: The fixed order is a design choice of the policy, not a measured ranking; the reason code TIE_BREAK_ORDER marks a decision made this way, BEST_SCORE a clear winner.
entries.keywords: tie break tie-break epsilon order reason code TIE_BREAK_ORDER BEST_SCORE equal scores fixed order deterministic

entries.title: Manual override in the Steganography Lab
entries.mechanics: An operator may force one algorithm in the Lab; the forced candidate is still checked for capacity, trial-encoded and tested against the hard limits, and the reason code is MANUAL_OVERRIDE.
entries.capacity: A forced algorithm whose capacity is too small is refused.
entries.distortion: A forced algorithm may produce more distortion than the policy choice, and the selection report shows the candidate table so the difference is visible.
entries.cost: The cost is that of a normal selection because every candidate is still analysed for the report.
entries.limitations: A manual override cannot bypass safety checks; an ineligible forced algorithm fails with ALGORITHM_NOT_ELIGIBLE and nothing is sent in plaintext.
entries.keywords: manual override forced algorithm lab operator MANUAL_OVERRIDE safety check refuse not eligible

entries.title: Webcam cover image
entries.mechanics: The cover is a webcam frame: either captured in the browser (getUserMedia, one frame drawn to a canvas, uploaded as a lossless PNG and re-encoded by the service) or captured by the Python service through OpenCV when it is available; the frame is saved as a cover artifact and used as the carrier for embedding.
entries.capacity: Capacity depends on the captured resolution and content; textured natural scenes give more edge-adaptive capacity than flat ones.
entries.distortion: Natural covers contain noise and gradients that mask small changes, so distortion is usually lower than on synthetic covers.
entries.cost: Capture adds camera latency before selection starts.
entries.limitations: The browser path needs a secure context such as localhost and camera permission, and the OpenCV path needs the optional OpenCV package; neither has been verified on a physical camera here, and when no webcam frame is available the procedural fallback is used instead of an error.
entries.keywords: webcam camera cover capture opencv natural image texture fallback device unverified hardware browser getusermedia canvas upload png browser_webcam uploaded permission secure context

entries.title: Procedural black and white cover
entries.mechanics: When no webcam image is available the service generates a deterministic procedural black and white cover image and records that the fallback was used.
entries.capacity: Capacity is predictable from the generated size, but flat saturated regions offer little edge capacity.
entries.distortion: Saturated pixels at 0 and 255 leave little room for changes, so lsb_matching must force its direction and some embeddings are refused.
entries.cost: Generation is cheap and needs no hardware.
entries.limitations: dct is typically ineligible on this cover because saturated blocks fail verification with ENCODE_VERIFY_FAILED; the fallback exists to keep the simulation usable, not to give good steganographic cover.
entries.keywords: procedural black white fallback generated cover synthetic saturated dct refused deterministic no camera

entries.title: Frame v1 and metadata authentication
entries.mechanics: The embedded frame is a 12-byte header, the AppWire bytes and a 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 tag computed with a key derived by HKDF-SHA256 from the directional AEAD key, so the tag is separate from the AEAD key.
entries.capacity: The frame adds 44 bytes of overhead to the AppWire, which counts against capacity.
entries.distortion: The frame is hidden in the cover like any payload; the tag itself does not change distortion beyond the extra bits.
entries.cost: Verification is one HMAC computation and a constant-time comparison on the receiver.
entries.limitations: A checksum is not authentication; the tag is verified before the AppWire is parsed, and the steganography layer gives no confidentiality beyond the AEAD already applied.
entries.keywords: frame header hmac sha256 tag hkdf metadata authentication key derivation appwire aead overhead verify before parse

entries.title: Bootstrap header
entries.mechanics: A 16-byte bootstrap with magic, version, algorithm id, parameter, frame length and a CRC32 is written into the least significant bits of samples 0 to 127 so the receiver knows which algorithm and length to extract.
entries.capacity: The bootstrap occupies the first 128 samples for every algorithm, which is why payload embedding starts at sample 128.
entries.distortion: It changes at most 128 samples by one level.
entries.cost: Reading it costs almost nothing and it is validated before extraction starts.
entries.limitations: The bootstrap is not authenticated by itself; the receiver compares it with the authenticated frame header and rejects a mismatch with FRAME_ALGORITHM_MISMATCH.
entries.keywords: bootstrap header crc32 algorithm id frame length samples 128 magic version validate mismatch receiver

entries.title: Detectability and robustness limits
entries.mechanics: All ten algorithms hide data in pixel values or transform coefficients of a lossless PNG and none adds error correction.
entries.capacity: Embedding more bits makes statistical detection easier for every method.
entries.distortion: Low PSNR change does not imply that statistical steganalysis fails.
entries.cost: No algorithm here spends effort on resisting steganalysis.
entries.limitations: None of the algorithms is claimed robust or undetectable: JPEG, resizing, cropping and filtering destroy the payload and the receiver fails closed, and modern steganalysis may detect LSB-class and PVD embedding.
entries.keywords: detectability steganalysis robustness limits jpeg resize crop filter fail closed undetectable not claimed honest limitation

entries.title: Selection and encoding failure codes
entries.mechanics: A candidate can be excluded for capacity, for exceeding the MSE, PSNR or cost limits, or because its trial encode fails verification.
entries.capacity: CAPACITY_INSUFFICIENT and EDGE_CAPACITY_INSUFFICIENT mean the frame does not fit; edge_adaptive_lsb never falls back to smooth pixels.
entries.distortion: ENCODE_VERIFY_FAILED means the decoded block or sample did not match what was embedded, as can happen for dct on saturated covers.
entries.cost: NO_ELIGIBLE_ALGORITHM is raised when every candidate is excluded and ALGORITHM_NOT_ELIGIBLE when a forced algorithm is excluded.
entries.limitations: Failures are returned as structured errors and recorded as events; there is never a silent passthrough or plaintext fallback.
entries.keywords: failure error code NO_ELIGIBLE_ALGORITHM ALGORITHM_NOT_ELIGIBLE CAPACITY_INSUFFICIENT ENCODE_VERIFY_FAILED exclusion structured event fail closed

entries.title: Role of this explanation
entries.mechanics: The explanation is produced after the selector has decided, from the selection report and this curated knowledge base, using word-overlap retrieval and a template with a claim check.
entries.capacity: It can mention only figures and algorithms present in the evidence it was given.
entries.distortion: It does not change distortion, score or any measured value.
entries.cost: It is optional: if it fails or is unavailable, the message is still delivered with a rule-based fallback explanation.
entries.limitations: The explanation is simulated, not a language model; it must not select, rank or veto an algorithm, and Rust accepts it only if the selected algorithm is echoed unchanged.
entries.keywords: rag explanation role simulated retrieval template claim check selected unchanged fallback optional outage not decision

entries.title: One-level Haar DWT QIM (dwt)
entries.mechanics: dwt splits one plane into 2x2 blocks, computes the orthonormal Haar coefficient HH = (a-b-c+d)/2 and moves it to the nearest multiple of the step delta, 4 by default, whose index parity equals the payload bit; after rounding each block is re-checked and alternative pixel patterns are tried near 0 and 255.
entries.capacity: dwt carries one bit per 2x2 block of the embedding plane, excluding the block rows that hold the bootstrap.
entries.distortion: Each block changes HH by at most two quantisation steps, spread over four pixels; distortion is moderate and higher than the LSB family.
entries.cost: Cost is low: a vectorised Haar step and verification per block.
entries.limitations: dwt is a transform-domain method but is not claimed robust to JPEG or resizing in this implementation; the lossless PNG hand-off is still required.
entries.keywords: dwt haar wavelet hh subband qim quantisation index modulation block 2x2 transform

entries.title: DCT-SVD singular-value QIM (dct_svd)
entries.mechanics: dct_svd applies an 8x8 orthonormal DCT, takes the 4x4 coefficient sub-matrix without the DC row and column, computes its SVD and quantises the largest singular value with step 16 by default so that the index parity equals the payload bit, then reconstructs and verifies each block.
entries.capacity: dct_svd carries one bit per 8x8 block, the lowest capacity of the ten algorithms, so small covers often cannot hold a frame.
entries.distortion: Changing the largest singular value moves the block by up to one quantisation step in the Frobenius norm, spread over 64 pixels.
entries.cost: Cost is moderate: one DCT, one 4x4 SVD and a verification per block.
entries.limitations: dct_svd is one concrete variant of the DCT-SVD family, not a universal DCT-SVD algorithm, and it is not claimed robust to JPEG or resizing here.
entries.keywords: dct svd singular value decomposition block 8x8 sigma quantisation transform variant

entries.title: HUGO with syndrome-trellis coding (hugo)
entries.mechanics: hugo computes, for every used sample, the exact change of the HUGO distortion, a weighted difference of co-occurrences of three consecutive pixel differences in eight directions with T 90, when the sample changes by plus or minus 1, and embeds with binary syndrome-trellis codes so that the total cost is minimal.
entries.capacity: hugo uses at most 131072 samples per image with a code rate of at least 1 bit per 2 samples; the automatic rate uses up to 10 samples per bit.
entries.distortion: Changes are plus or minus 1 and are concentrated where the co-occurrence model changes least, giving very low distortion for small frames.
entries.cost: Cost is the highest of the ten: per-sample HUGO cost evaluation plus a Viterbi search over 128 trellis states.
entries.limitations: This hugo uses the additive single-change approximation without model correction, so it is a named variant of HUGO, and low distortion does not mean undetectable.
entries.keywords: hugo high dimensional model spam co-occurrence distortion stc syndrome trellis adaptive cost

entries.title: WOW with syndrome-trellis coding (wow)
entries.mechanics: wow filters the cover with three directional Daubechies-8 wavelet filters, measures embedding suitability as the filtered residual magnitude, combines the three directions with a reciprocal sum so that smooth directions dominate the cost, and embeds with binary syndrome-trellis codes.
entries.capacity: wow uses at most 131072 samples per image with a code rate of at least 1 bit per 2 samples.
entries.distortion: Changes are plus or minus 1 and avoid smooth regions and clean edges, which keeps distortion very low for small frames.
entries.cost: Cost is high: three filter passes per channel plus a Viterbi search.
entries.limitations: wow is fragile to JPEG, resizing and filtering, and distortion minimisation is not proof of undetectability.
entries.keywords: wow wavelet obtained weights directional filter db8 suitability cost map stc adaptive

entries.title: S-UNIWARD with syndrome-trellis coding (s_uniward)
entries.mechanics: s_uniward computes the spatial UNIWARD cost, the sum over three directional Daubechies-8 wavelet filters of the reciprocal of 1 plus the residual magnitude convolved with the absolute filter, and embeds with binary syndrome-trellis codes.
entries.capacity: s_uniward uses at most 131072 samples per image with a code rate of at least 1 bit per 2 samples.
entries.distortion: Changes are plus or minus 1 and are placed where wavelet coefficients change least in relative terms, giving very low distortion for small frames.
entries.cost: Cost is high: three filter passes per channel plus a Viterbi search.
entries.limitations: This is the spatial variant S-UNIWARD, not J-UNIWARD; it is fragile to lossy processing and distortion minimisation is not proof of undetectability.
entries.keywords: s_uniward uniward universal wavelet relative distortion sigma spatial db8 stc adaptive

entries.title: Syndrome-trellis codes
entries.mechanics: Syndrome-trellis codes embed a message as the syndrome of a sparse parity-check matrix and use a Viterbi search to find the stego bits with minimal total cost; this project uses binary codes with constraint height 7.
entries.capacity: The code rate is message bits divided by used samples; the receiver needs only the stego bits, the rate and the matrix seed.
entries.distortion: STC minimises the sum of per-sample costs, so its benefit depends entirely on the cost map.
entries.cost: The Viterbi search costs about 128 operations per used sample.
entries.limitations: STC is used only for the additive cost formulations of hugo, wow and s_uniward; the submatrices are generated deterministically and are not the published optimised ones, so some coding loss is expected.
entries.keywords: stc syndrome trellis code viterbi parity check rate constraint height coding loss
